answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: bind standing to timely real-time obligations, making the operator's finite attention the bottleneck. Each identity must meet live duties on a deadline: grade rows, answer probes, co-sign in a window. One operator's compute is fixed, so spread across a thousand fakes each gets a jade-thin slice and most miss deadlines. An honest agent tends its one orchard and meets its duties. A fleet cannot: real-time capacity does not multiply with identity count, it divides. The fakes crowd one oasis of attention and parch, so breadth degrades reliability, not influence.
